solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: As before, observe flood in which fish flips over

definitions.note: 'As before' marks an obsolete sense of the verb

indicators.note: something that flips over ends up facing the other way, so the fish is written backwards
'in which' says the flood holds the next item inside it

blocks.note: a spate is a sudden flood of a river
the luce is an old name for the pike

explanation.surface: An angler watches a river in spate where a fish is leaping and turning over.
explanation.walkthrough: SPECULATE once meant simply to look at or observe, from Latin specula, a watchtower.
explanation.definitionFit: The older meaning of speculate was to view or watch closely, the sense 'as before' points to.

clue.text: Vagrant in street, exhausted person

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for street
someone worn out is 'a rag' — limp and spent

explanation.surface: A tramp lies on the street, completely worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: A strag is a dialect word for a straggler or stray, someone wandering without a fixed place.

clue.text: Old characters in NZ settlement with toilet on island

blocks.note: a pa or pah is a fortified Maori village in New Zealand
short for lavatory
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A traveller describes an old-fashioned Maori village with a lavatory on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with ... on' simply places the toilet and island after the settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: Pahlavi is the script used for Middle Persian writing, so the word names a set of ancient written characters.

clue.text: Satire performed receives stick? The opposite

indicators.note: to receive is to take in, so one item ends up holding the other
this flips the stated relation, so the stick does the holding instead of being held

blocks.note: a cane is a walking stick
to perform a task is to do it

explanation.surface: A theatre note: the satire, once staged, gets a beating from the critics.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'performed receives stick' puts the stick inside; 'The opposite' tells you the stick does the receiving, holding the performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Candide is Voltaire's famous satirical novel mocking blind optimism, a classic example of satire.

clue.text: This old language sounds dull

indicators.note: 'sounds' tells you to go by how a word is pronounced rather than spelt

blocks.note: leaden means heavy and dull

explanation.surface: A complaint that some archaic tongue is tedious to listen to.
explanation.definitionFit: Ledden is an archaic word for a language or speech, found in Spenser and older poetry.

clue.text: A second degree restricts one ultimately — one doesn't have much of a life!

definitions.text: one doesn't have much of a life!

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter is used
to restrict is to hem in, so the outer words close around the selected letter

blocks.note: taken as written
a mo is a moment, a second
Bachelor of Arts, a university degree
the last letter of 'one'

explanation.surface: A disparaging remark about someone with a second-class degree who leads a dull life.
explanation.walkthrough: The E sits between the second and the degree; the exclamation mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoeba is a single-celled organism, about the simplest form of existence — hardly a full life.

clue.text: I'm in a financial scheme with others — there's money in cosmetic stuff

definitions.text: I'm in a financial scheme with others

indicators.note: 'there's X in Y' puts the first item inside the second

blocks.note: toner is a skin lotion used as a cosmetic
tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: A saver boasts of joining a group investment that profits from the beauty industry.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is written in the first person: the answer is speaking of itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A tontiner is a subscriber to a tontine, an annuity scheme where survivors' shares grow as members die.

clue.text: Proper friend in the first place

blocks.note: prim means stiffly proper
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Someone recalls that a strait-laced friend was first to arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: Primally means originally or primarily, which is what 'in the first place' expresses.

clue.text: 'ampshire town as before

definitions.note: an obsolete adverb meaning before, in front

indicators.note: the county is spelt the way a dropped-aitch speaker says it, so the town loses its first letter in the same way

blocks.note: Havant is a town in Hampshire

explanation.surface: A local, dropping aitches, names a Hampshire town just as earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampshire is a county on England's south coast; the apostrophe teaches the trick by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Avant is an obsolete form meaning before or in front, as in avant-garde, the old use 'as before' points to.

clue.text: Cheese in cake always

blocks.note: a pan is a hard cake of pressed matter, as in pancake make-up or a salt pan crust
e'er is the poetic short form of ever

explanation.surface: A cook claims there is always cheese in the cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Paneer is the fresh unsalted cheese used in South Asian cooking.

clue.text: Word of appreciation by fellow for meat dish

blocks.note: ta is British informal for thanks
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A diner thanks a man who brought the meat course.
explanation.definitionFit: A tamale is a Mexican dish of seasoned meat wrapped in maize dough and steamed in a husk.

clue.text: Fibrous plant in very small area east of heath

blocks.note: a moor is open heathland
V is the abbreviation for very
A abbreviates area, 'small' signalling the shortening

explanation.surface: A botanist notes a stringy plant growing in a tiny patch beside the heath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'east of' puts the small area after the heath, since across clues read west to east.
explanation.definitionFit: Moorva is the bowstring hemp of India, a plant grown for its strong fibre.

clue.text: Money pursued by academic sharks

blocks.note: rhino is old slang for money
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: Money-lenders and loan sharks hound a lecturer for cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharks' looks like crooks in the surface but is the literal fish; Rhinodon is the whale shark's old genus name.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhinodon is the genus name once given to the whale shark, so the word names those sharks.

clue.text: Follower of Jesus in Chinese city

blocks.note: first meaning: an abbreviation of Christian, the X standing for the Greek chi
second meaning: ..., the city of the terracotta army

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a Christian living in China; the city is the one famous for the terracotta warriors.
explanation.definitionFit: Xian is a written abbreviation for a Christian believer and also the name of a major historic city in Shaanxi.

clue.text: A story about the old man that took astronomical measurements

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the thing that took them

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so the story surrounds the next item

blocks.note: taken as written
a story can be a lie, a fib
one's old man is one's father

explanation.surface: A tale about father, who used to measure the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: An alidade is a sighting rule used on astrolabes and plane tables for measuring angles, including to stars.

clue.text: Language of old group of people enthralling a number

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so the group holds the number within it

blocks.note: teme is an archaic form of team, a group
N stands for an unspecified number in algebra

explanation.surface: A historian studies the tongue of a past people who were captivated by one figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Temne is a language of Sierra Leone, spoken by the Temne people.

clue.text: Is everything found in a last resort?

indicators.note: something found in another sits inside it

blocks.note: per means 'a', as in fifty miles per hour
taken as written
all means everything

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker asks whether a final-choice hotel provides absolutely everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a last resort' reads as a phrase, but 'a' must be split off to supply the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Pis aller is French for 'worse going', a course taken when nothing better is available.

clue.text: Position of soldier that's horrible without support — start to panic

indicators.note: 'without' in its old sense means outside, so the exclamation wraps around
the start of a word is its first letter, so only that is taken

blocks.note: fie is an exclamation of disgust
a rest is a support, as for a cue or rifle
the first letter of panic

explanation.surface: A soldier in a dreadful position without backing begins to panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's horrible' is not a description but the exclamation itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire-step is a ledge in a trench on which a soldier stands to fire over the parapet.

clue.text: Growing as twins at home beset by rage

indicators.note: to be beset by something is to be surrounded by it

blocks.note: bate is an old word for rage or temper
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: Twins growing up at home amid constant fury.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany, binate describes leaves that grow in pairs from a single point.

clue.text: Invalid sadly losing pounds — protein required

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away
sadly suggests things have gone badly wrong, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
L, from libra, is the symbol for pounds

explanation.surface: A sick patient who has lost weight is told to eat more protein.
explanation.walkthrough: Pounds are both body weight in the surface and the letter L in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Avidin is a protein in egg white that binds biotin tightly.

clue.text: Polish nails inappropriately inside quiet hotel

indicators.note: done inappropriately means done wrongly, so the letters are put in the wrong order
inside places the reworked letters within the outer pair

blocks.note: p, piano, means quietly in music
taken as written
H is Hotel in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A manicurist at a hushed hotel varnishes nails badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' tempts as nationality or nail varnish; it is the verb to make smooth.
explanation.definitionFit: To planish is to smooth or flatten metal by hammering or rolling, giving it a polished surface.

clue.text: Invention with one not quiet showing vanity

indicators.note: the soft-signal letter is removed and the numeral for one put in its place

blocks.note: a concept is an idea, a mental invention
I is the Roman numeral for one
p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet

explanation.surface: An inventor who will not keep quiet shows how vain they are.
explanation.definitionFit: Conceit is excessive pride in oneself, which is what vanity means.

clue.text: Flog WI produce maybe — second-rate/satisfactory?

blocks.note: the Women's Institute, a British rural women's club, is famed for making jam
B grade is second-rate
OK means acceptable

explanation.surface: Should one sell the WI's homemade goods — are they mediocre or just about passable?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flog' looks like sell, but means whip.
explanation.definitionFit: A jambok (sjambok) is a heavy South African hide whip, and as a verb it means to flog with one.

clue.text: Some viewers' areas had planned activities time set up

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: to have a meal is to eat it
the initial letters of these two words
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A TV schedule note that some regions have had their programmed events moved.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials are taken without a separate signal, a liberty some advanced puzzles allow. Viewers are eyes here.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapeta are reflective layers behind the retina in some animals' eyes, helping night vision — areas of those viewers.

clue.text: Unpopular doctor with pained expression, college type

blocks.note: Dr Fell is the man in the rhyme 'I do not love thee, Dr Fell'
ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: A disliked physician grimaces at a member of a university.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow is a senior member of a college, one of its governing body.

clue.text: Less inclined to show bias as female broadcaster?

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
one who airs or broadcasts

explanation.surface: A woman presenter is said to be more impartial.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairer is the comparative of fair in its sense of just and impartial.

clue.text: Spiders one's found in region

indicators.note: to be found in something is to be inside it

blocks.note: an area is a region
an is the indefinite article meaning one; 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A naturalist notes that one spider is found in each region.
explanation.definitionFit: Aranea is the Latin name for spider, used for the genus of orb-weaving spiders.

clue.text: Big old footballing boy keeping order

indicators.note: to keep is to hold, so the boy holds the honour inside

blocks.note: Roy of the Rovers was a long-running British comic-strip footballer
the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A large veteran footballer is honoured with a decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Roomy means spacious, having plenty of room, so big in capacity.

clue.text: Old soldier, a bit of a nut left to pass away

indicators.note: passing away means disappearing, so that letter goes

blocks.note: a kernel is the inner part of a nut
L for left

explanation.surface: A veteran, a bit of a crank, is left to die.
explanation.definitionFit: A kerne was a light-armed Irish or Highland foot soldier of the Middle Ages.

clue.text: Spots patterns

blocks.note: first meaning: marks or stains, as in iron-mold
second meaning: shapes for casting, the American spelling of moulds

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are nouns; the spelling is the American one.
explanation.definitionFit: Mold can mean a discolouring spot or stain, and also a template or shape that forms a pattern.

clue.text: Vessel making speed interrupted by bar

indicators.note: something interrupted is broken into, so the bar goes in the middle

blocks.note: pace is speed
an inn is a pub, a bar

explanation.surface: A boat's progress is held up by a sandbar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a sandbank in a nautical scene, but it is a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnace is a small boat carried by a larger ship, or a light sailing vessel.

clue.text: Playwright's run

blocks.note: first meaning: Robert ..., author of A Man for All Seasons
second meaning: to dash off suddenly

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a playwright's theatre run; the 's is 'is', linking the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Bolt was an English dramatist, and to bolt is to run away fast.

clue.text: Time to face mistake about charge — legal resolution needed

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so the mistake wraps the charge

blocks.note: T stands for time
to err is to make a mistake
a mine is an explosive charge

explanation.surface: A defendant must face a wrongful charge before the case can be settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to face' puts time in front. 'charge' tempts as a criminal charge, but it is explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: Terminer, as in the old courts of oyer and terminer, means a hearing and determining of a legal case.

clue.text: American food in small East End home we fancy?

indicators.note: Cockneys of London's East End drop their aitches, making the word smaller

blocks.note: taken as written
'let' as in 'let it be so' — we suppose or imagine

explanation.surface: An imagined cosy East End house serving American dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: The American spelling is signalled by the definition; East End speech, dropping the H, gives 'ome.
explanation.definitionFit: Omelet is the US spelling of omelette, a dish of beaten eggs.

clue.text: What could be boring for Scot? Terrible English — no good!

definitions.text: What could be boring for Scot?

indicators.note: 'no' says the following item is absent
something terrible is badly mangled, so its letters are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written
G for good

explanation.surface: A Scot finds bad English tedious and worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like tedious, but it means making holes.
explanation.definitionFit: An elshin is the Scots word for a shoemaker's awl, a tool for boring holes.

clue.text: Record chief troublemaker in Greek province

blocks.note: an EP is an extended-play record
arch means chief, as in archenemy
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: A leading agitator in a Greek region is put on record.
explanation.definitionFit: An eparchate, or eparchy, is a province of ancient or modern Greece governed by an eparch.
